texto_aprovado: Then, about 23 million years ago, Australia's leading edge began running into Southeast Asia, and a chain of islands formed between the two. On a map, those islands look like stepping stones. Very few mammals ever made it across them. The only ones that crossed on their own and took hold were rodents and bats.
